subject: Private inference for HealthSecure — discovery notes & next steps
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Asha Kapoor <asha.kapoor@healthsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Private inference for HealthSecure — discovery notes & next steps

Hi Asha — thanks again for carving out 30 minutes today. Quick recap from our side to make sure I captured the requirements correctly and call out proposed next steps. If I missed anything, please flag.

Summary of pain and goals
- Regulated workloads (PHI) require data never to leave HealthSecure control zone; primary objective is to host inference in a VPC/on-prem environment with strong key management and audit trails.
- Current pain: slow turnaround for model-driven features (NLP triage) because infra teams are running experiments on a fragmented on-prem infra; they need predictable latency and throughput for patient-facing flows.
- Compliance constraints: SOC2 evidence, quarterly pen-test attestation, and 7+ year audit log retention for access and inference events.

Current stack you described
- On-prem VMware cluster + private OpenShift (v4.12) for critical workloads.
- Primary identity: Okta SSO; existing KMS is an HSM appliance (Thales) used for DB encryption.
- Egress policy: extremely restrictive — only allow-listed outbound IP ranges; no direct internet access from inference hosts today.

Success criteria (what will make this a win)
- Deployable within HealthSecure network (VPC peering / private connectivity) or an on-prem appliance that meets air-gap requirements.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK) with HSM integration and offline key import/rotation workflows.
- P95 latency < 250ms for 512-token prompts at target concurrency (initial target 200 req/s).
- Full audit trail for inference requests (per-token metadata) retained for 7+ years and accessible for audits.
- Deterministic deployment path for procurement (clear SLAs and pricing for Dedicated vs Private).

Risks / open questions
- Network: will the infra team allow outbound TLS to vendor endpoints if IP allow-listing is provided, or do we need an air-gapped, on-prem runtime?
- Data residency: all logs and model artifacts must remain in HealthSecure's environment — confirm whether a private control plane is acceptable.
- KMS: details on HSM API and offline key transfer process needed to validate BYOK.

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan)
1) I will share our Private/VPC requirements questionnaire and a short checklist for network allow-listing (attached). (action: Jonas)
2) HealthSecure to confirm procurement timeline and whether IT will accept IP allow-listing or requires fully air-gapped runtime. (action: Asha)
3) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rafael (solutions engineer) and your infra/security engineers to review HSM integration and key rotation. Rafael suggested Tue/Thu mornings this week — please confirm availability. (action: Marissa + Asha)
4) We will prepare an initial sizing estimate and SLA comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) once we have HSM API details and expected QPS. (action: Jonas)

Attachments: healthsecure_private_requirements_v1.xlsx (questionnaire), redwood_sla_draft_20260418.pdf (SLA/pricing starter).

Thanks — happy to hop on another quick sync if helpful.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Thanks for the thorough summary, Jonas — this matches my notes and is very helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Network: our default approach is to avoid vendor internet egress. We can accept allow-listed outbound to specific IPs if it's a short list and approved by our networking team; otherwise we will require an air-gapped option for the inference runtime.
- HSM: yes, we use a Thales Luna HSM. We support PKCS#11 and an offline key-import workflow. I'll ask IT for the HSM spec sheet and share.
- Timeline: Procurement kickoff is targeted for end of May; security review will begin mid-May. We would like to evaluate a pilot by late June if feasible.

Next: I'll loop in our lead infra engineer (CC'd to procurement) once I have their availability. Can Rafael send a short agenda for the technical deep-dive so we can prep the right folks?

Asha

Hi Asha, Jonas — Rafael here, solutions engineering. Thanks for the context. Attached is a concise agenda and checklist I plan to run through during the deep-dive. High-level call plan:
1) 10m — Introductions & goals for pilot (confirm QPS, latency targets, dataset sensitivity)
2) 15m — HSM/BYOK: PKCS#11 endpoints, key provisioning and rotation, HSM network topologies (management vs appliance mode)
3) 10m — Network architecture options:
   - Option A: Private control plane with TLS to allow-listed IPs (requires minimal outbound egress and whitelisted CIDR)
   - Option B: Fully on-prem runtime (air-gapped) with physical media transfer for initial model artifacts and offline key import
4) 10m — Observability & audit plan (log format, S3-compatible on-prem storage, retention policy)
5) 5m — Next steps and MOUs (NDA, timeline)

Checklist items we'll request ahead of the call:
- HSM spec + PKCS#11 access details
- Network allow-listing policy / current egress controls
- Security questionnaire (we'll fill and return)

If Tue 10:00 PT works for you, I'll send a calendar invite and a short pre-read. Looking forward to it.

-Rafael
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
